audit_findings.title: Cash bridge ignores a known next-day $163 million repayment
audit_findings.magnitude: $163.0 million, equal to $4.63 per share, 40.1% of the $406.316 million cash bridge, and 5.5% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash without deducting debt, so cash used immediately after year-end to repay the Revolver cannot remain attributable to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: On July 1, 2026, we repaid the outstanding borrowings of $ 163.0 million on the Revolver.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing error. Removing $163.0 million reduces base value from $84.36 to approximately $79.73 per share and the buy-below level from $59.05 to approximately $55.81. It does not reverse the conclusion that the shares are above even bull value, but it materially changes the stated intrinsic-value and purchase thresholds.
audit_findings.action: Rerun every scenario with post-repayment cash, reducing the additive cash bridge by $163.0 million while continuing not to deduct the repaid Revolver principal.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include tuition advances that are not excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $406.316 million gross cash versus $259.125 million current deferred revenue, including $48.5 million of material-right liabilities; required adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge treats all cash as a separable non-operating asset even though some cash may fund instruction, refunds, scholarships, and seasonal working-capital obligations already represented in future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Deferred revenue within current liabilities is $ 259.1 million and $ 214.1 million as of June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, which includes $ 48.5 million and $ 38.1 million as of June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, related to contract liabilities associated with material rights.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial advance collections and seasonal cash flows, but it does not identify the distributable excess-cash amount. Deferred revenue cannot automatically be deducted dollar-for-dollar because the remaining cost of providing instruction is less than the recorded revenue liability. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Build a monthly cash and working-capital schedule by institution, identify cash associated with unperformed terms, refunds and material rights, establish a minimum operating-cash reserve, and rerun the bridge using only verified excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Legacy DeVry liabilities may be excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 discontinued-operations loss of $21.236 million pre-tax and $15.809 million after tax; $340.0 million contractual Liability Cap; remaining exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Legal payments omitted from continuing-operations OE would reduce annual owner earnings; probable liabilities not captured in OE would require a separate equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: As previously disclosed, pursuant to the terms of the Stock Purchase Agreement by and between Covista and Cogswell, dated as of December 4, 2017, as amended, Covista sold DeVry University to Cogswell and Covista agreed to indemnify DeVry University for certain losses up to $ 340.0 million (the “Liability Cap”).
audit_findings.explanation: A fiscal-2026 discontinued-operations loss and continuing legacy litigation are demonstrated, and the $15.809 million after-tax loss equals 8.7% of the $182.3 million OE anchor. The record does not establish how much was cash, whether the OE series retained it, whether costs will recur, or how much of the Liability Cap remains. The $340.0 million cap is a ceiling, not a demonstrated liability.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to total-company cash flows including discontinued operations, obtain the Liability Cap utilization ledger and legal accrual analysis, then normalize recurring cash costs or deduct probable uncapitalized exposure and rerun.

audit_findings.title: Post-anchor federal-loan restrictions may break the growth assumptions
audit_findings.magnitude: 78% of revenue depends on federal education assistance; valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Lower funding availability could reduce enrollment, persistence, tuition realization and margins, lowering both forecast OE and sustainable growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Recent changes to federal student loan programs that reduce annual, aggregate, and lifetime borrowing limits and limit federal student aid for part-time students may limit students’ ability to finance their education, which may in turn materially and adversely affect our results of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking risk beginning immediately after the historical anchor. The filing supports substantial exposure but provides no observed post-effective-date financial results. The zero-growth bear case does not necessarily capture an OE contraction, while the 3% and 6% growth cases may be too high if funding gaps materially affect students.
audit_findings.action: Collect post-July 1, 2026 applications, starts, persistence, funding gaps and private-financing approval data by institution and program; then rerun scenarios with institution-specific enrollment, pricing, credit-loss and margin effects, including a declining-OE bear case.

audit_findings.title: Thousands of BDR claims create an unmodeled recoupment tail
audit_findings.mechanism: Approved claims could create cash recoupments or security requirements that reduce OE, require an equity-bridge liability, or restrict capital available for operations and shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 30, 2026, AUC, Chamberlain, RUSM, RUSVM, and Walden respectively have received 390 , 3,224 , 1,958 , 2,020 , and 9,031 BDR claims.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim inventory is demonstrated and already exists, so this is more than a generic future risk. However, no institution had received an approval or recoupment notice, and the filing supplies neither claimed principal nor approval probabilities. The record therefore cannot establish a recognizable liability or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain claimed principal by institution and cohort, remove duplicate or overlapping claims, document approval and recoupment experience, assess defenses and coverage, and rerun the bridge and OE under supportable recoupment and letter-of-credit scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The stated share-count ceiling may not be a true PSU ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: 528,174 unvested PSUs, equal to 1.50% of the 35.173617 million-share denominator; additional maximum shares unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional PSU settlement shares would increase the fully diluted denominator and reduce value per share without changing enterprise or equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The final number of shares that vest under our PSUs is based on metrics approved by the Compensation Committee of the Board.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that PSU quantities can increase because 196,416 incremental PSUs were recorded during fiscal 2026 based on metric achievement. It does not disclose whether the current 528,174 balance represents target, estimated or maximum settlement. Thus the claimed no-offset ceiling is unsupported, but the incremental dilution cannot be quantified from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Review the fiscal-2025 and fiscal-2026 PSU award agreements for maximum payout multipliers, calculate maximum shares issuable for every outstanding tranche, replace estimated PSU units with that ceiling, and rerun per-share values.
